title: Origin | Roots
location: 4Roots Farm Campus, 1101 N. John Young Parkway, Parkway Orlando
description: Origin invites guests to experience not simply what is on the plate, but everything that came before it. Nestled among the gardens and fields of the 4Roots Farm Campus, Origin is an intimate dining experience where the story of every remarkable meal begins. In partnership with a celebrated guest chef, a local farmer, and 4Roots’ Chef Hari Pulapaka, each dinner is a unique exploration of the season—never repeated, and rooted in what the land has to offer at that moment. Origin is more than fine dining. It is an invitation to experience food with a deeper sense of wonder. Not simply where food is served. But where its story begins. This Month’s Theme & Featured Chef The Origin season begins with Roots , a celebration of the agricultural foundations of our region through autumn harvests and timeless cooking traditions. This one-night-only dining inaugural dinner features acclaimed Central Florida chef Kevin Fonzo , a James Beard Award semifinalist and one of Orlando’s original pioneers of the local food movement. Event Details Date: Thursday, October 1st Location: 4Roots Farm Campus – Food Forest Lawn + Barn Time: 6:00pm – 9:00pm Tickets: $175 per guest. Each ticket purchase supports local farms and the mission of 4Roots to create greater food access and education in our community.

title: 2nd Annual Farm to Healthcare: 2026 CME Conference
location: 4Roots Farm Campus, 1101 N. John Young Parkway, Parkway Orlando
description: Join the Culinary Health Institute at 4Roots Farm for the 2nd Annual Farm to Health Continuing Medical Education (CME) Conference, a one-of-a-kind educational experience designed for health professionals passionate about whole-person, food-forward care. This immersive conference is presented by the Ardmore Institute of Health (AIH) and is part of the Florida Food is Medicine Partnership Series, following Day 1: The 4th Annual Food is Medicine Symposium on October 8 in Winter Park, Florida. Bringing together physicians, dietitians, faculty, and allied health professionals, this program explores Food as Medicine, lifestyle-based care, and culinary medicine through evidence-based lectures and hands-on, experiential learning. Limited seating is available. Hosted by Dr. Arianna Becker , the program features a team of experienced healthcare and culinary experts exploring the role of food as medicine in clinical and community settings. Benefits of Attending: Earn AMA PRA Category 1 Credit(s)™ through an accredited, evidence-based program Gain practical, clinical applications of Food as Medicine, Lifestyle Medicine, and Shared Medical Appointments Participate in hands-on culinary and experiential learning sessions Learn from nationally recognized physicians, dietitians, and faculty Network with interdisciplinary health professionals in an immersive farm-based setting Receive a Culinary Health Institute (CHI) Certificate of Completion for the Culinary Health Essentials Take home a limited-edition CHI tote bag Full program details and registration are available on our website . Register today to take advantage of early bird pricing through July 31, 2026 using promo code: EARLYBIRD26 Register today at 4rootsfarm.org/cme

title: Make & Take- Nature’s Brew Tea Blending Workshop
location: 4Roots Farm Campus, 1101 N. John Young Parkway, Parkway Orlando
description: Join us at the 4Roots Farm Campus for a hands-on Make & Take Workshop where you’ll craft your own custom tea blends using fresh herbs and plants from our farm! In this interactive class, you’ll learn how to create unique, aromatic tea blends while exploring the vital role of plants in our ecosystem and their medicinal properties. During this guided experience, you’ll delve into the art of blending teas, understanding how to combine various herbs and plants to create delicious and beneficial infusions. Our team will lead you through each step, sharing insights about the benefits of different botanicals and the importance of sustainable farming practices. We’ll start with a brief introduction to our herb gardens, highlighting the fascinating properties of various plants and their contribution to health and wellness. Then, it’s time to create: each participant will craft a custom tea blend to take home, along with the knowledge to continue making these natural infusions at home. 🗓️ Saturday, October 10th | 10:30am – 12:00pm 📍 4Roots Farm Campus – Education Building: 1101 N. John Young Pkwy, Orlando, FL 32804 🎟️ $35 Admission 🌿 All materials & supplies included! Please Note: Anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an adult.

title: Food as Medicine: Eating Well for Breast Cancer Prevention
location: Center for Health and Wellbeing, 2005 Mizell Ave #800, Winter Park
description: Presented by 4Root’s Culinary Health Institute at Center for Health & Wellbeing Explore the powerful connection between what’s on your plate and your overall health through our Food as Medicine chef and physician series! 🧑‍🍳🩺 Join the Culinary Health Institute and Dr. Amber Orman, double-board certified radiation oncologist, lifestyle medicine specialist, and AdventHealth Chief Wellness Officer, for an evening focused on the importance of healthy eating and sustainable lifestyle changes in the prevention of breast cancer and breast cancer recurrence. Guests will enjoy a three-course plant-based tasting menu prepared by Chef Nikk Burton, executive chef at the Monroe Restaurant , and learn valuable insights on plant-based nutrition, healthy lifestyle choices, and the powerful role food plays in obtaining a higher quality of life. What You’ll Experience Expert Guidance and Interactive Q&A with Dr. Amber Orman. Culinary Demonstration and Tasting of a 3-course plant-forward meal focused on reducing cancer risk using plant-based nutrition prepared by Chef Nikk Burton. Connection with other guests through conversation, shared ideas, and inspiration Event Details: 📆 Date & Time: Tuesday, October 13th | 6:00 PM – 8:00 PM 📍 Location: Center for Health & Wellbeing, 2005 Mizell Ave #800, Winter Park, FL 🎟️ Ticket Price: $60 per guest

title: Homeschool Day at 4Roots Farm (Ages 5-7)
location: 4Roots Farm Campus, 1101 N. John Young Parkway, Parkway Orlando
description: The 4Roots Homeschool Days program brings learning to life through hands-on experiences in the garden and beyond. Through seasonal, interactive activities, students explore agriculture and the environment in a way that encourages curiosity, creativity, and real-world connection. Designed for a range of ages, our program blends playful discovery with meaningful learning as students dive deeper into agriculture and related sciences. Each experience is designed to build practical skills while fostering a greater understanding of sustainability, engineering, and the natural world. October’s Theme: Prehistoric Plants and Peoples Get ready to travel back in time to learn about the ancient flora and fauna that lived alongside the dinosaurs! Take an up close look at living fossils growing on the farm and investigate how early pollinators and plant relationships have evolved over millions of years. Bringing history forward in time, learners will also step into the ingenuity of early Florida peoples, including the Calusa, as they explore how natural materials were used to create tools for daily life and gardening. Session activities: 🦕 Explore plants that lived during time of dinosaurs 📔Create a timeline of plant evolution using examples around the farm 🔎 Investigate plant adaptations over time 🌺 Dissect plant specimens and examine their anatomy

title: Edible Canvas Class: Plant-Based Edition
location: 4Roots Farm Campus, 1101 N. John Young Parkway, Parkway Orlando
description: Presented by 4Root’s Culinary Health Institute & Journey Across the Board Join Jon Barr, founder and owner of Journey Across the Board , for one of his signature edible canvas classes — “plant-based edition” ! In this interactive hands-on culinary art experience, Jon will teach you how to use simple ingredients such as plant-based cheese, colorful spreads, and 4Roots freshly harvested items to create an edible plant-based work of art on a mini-canvas. What You’ll Experience Learn how to transform plant-based ingredients into art using color, flavor, and texture in your design A fun new way to make plant-based spreads approachable even beyond the classroom Friendly and relaxed atmosphere ( No experience required) Hands-on interactive preparation of an edible mini-canvas Taste and enjoy your “artwork” during the class Note: This class is also gluten-free, soy free and carrageenan free Event Details 📍 Location: 4Roots Farm Campus – Education Building: 1101 N. John Young Parkway, Orlando, FL 32804 📅 Date: October 14 | 6:00PM – 7:00 PM 🎟️ Ticket Fee: $35 Meet Your Instructor Jon Barr, Founder & Owner of Journey Across the Board Jon Barr is the Owner and Founder of Journey Across the Board , where food, hospitality, and a little bit of showmanship come together around the table. A lifelong performer, Jon has spent nearly 30 years working as an actor and singer while simultaneously building a career in the food and hospitality world as a server, manager, trainer, and teacher. When the pandemic brought the entertainment industry to a standstill, Jon found himself looking for a new way to bring people together through the things he loved most. The result was Journey Across the Board. Jon approaches food with curiosity, flexibility, and a belief that there is no single “right” way to eat. His boards and grazing tables can follow any path, from carnivore to vegetarian to plant-based, with thoughtful options for allergies and dietary preferences. He prioritizes quality ingredients, including organic produce, exceptional meats and cheeses, and products from small-batch purveyors whenever possible. But for Jon, food is about more than flavor. Drawing from his background in performance, he believes every board should be a show of its own, combining beautiful presentation with unexpected flavors, textures, and opportunities for connection.

title: Tea Vitality Workshop: A Sensory Experience
description: Presented by 4Root’s Culinary Health Institute at Center for Health & Wellbeing Join the Culinary Health Institute and Julie Ward, plant-based, certified ACE health coach, and international speaker as she guides you in the exploration of the energizing and calming effect of herbal teas in one of her most popular classes.Participants will sample a variety of herbal tea blends and learn ways to focus the senses for maximizing the health benefits of tea. What You’ll Experience; · Learn about the benefits of herbal tea blends · Taste teas designed to provide energy and relax your mind · Discover how tea supports lower stress and anxiety Program Note: Participants with certain medical conditions or those taking blood thinners or other medications should consult with their physician prior to sampling herbal teas. Please notify the presenter before the session begins if you need to avoid specific herbs. Meet Julie Ward Julie Ward is the founder of Spirit Alchemy, a wellness education company focused on the integration of mind, body, and spirit through plant-based nutrition, herbalism, mindfulness, and spiritual wellness practices. An international speaker, educator, herbalist, and certified ACE Health Coach, Julie is known for creating experiences that help people feel more grounded, emotionally steady, and connected to themselves. Her work combines nervous system support, the healing qualities of plants, mindful awareness, and spiritual insight in a way that is both practical and deeply restorative. With a background in education and public policy, Julie has taught wellness programs and workshops for community organizations, colleges, corporations, and wellness centers. Her approach encourages participants to see health as more than physical wellness alone, but as an interconnected relationship between nourishment, rest, emotional well-being, beliefs, and spiritual alignment. Julie holds a certificate in Plant-Based Nutrition from eCornell, a Master’s degree in Public Policy from USC, and a B.S. in Mathematics from Spelman College. She is also an herbalist, plant-based chef, meditation facilitator, and Licensed Spiritual Practitioner through Agape International Spiritual Center. Through workshops, tea experiences, speaking engagements, and educational programs, Julie invites people to slow down, reconnect with themselves, and create lifestyle practices that support greater clarity, peace, and well-being. Event Details 📍 Location: Center for Health & Wellbeing – Nutrition Theatre: 2005 Mizell Ave, Winter Park, FL 32792 📅 Date: October 19th | 1:00PM – 2:00 PM 🎟️ Ticket Fee: $10 About the Culinary Health Institute at 4Roots Farm The Culinary Health Institute (CHI) is an initiative of 4Roots in partnership with AdventHealth, Florida Blue, and Gordon Food Service. CHI works to transform community health by advancing food as medicine and whole-person care through education, clinical innovation, and research. Learn more at 4rootsfarm.org/CHI .

title: Community Plant-Based Potluck
location: 4Roots Farm Campus, 1101 N. John Young Parkway, Parkway Orlando
description: Join a space where food meets creativity, flavor, and community. The Culinary Health Institute’s Monthly Community Potluck is rooted in sharing food and conversation, meeting new people, and sharing the journey of living a plant-based lifestyle. Whether you’re fully plant-based, plant-curious, or just love good food and good conversation, all are welcome to this free event. 🍽️ Bring a Dish: Please prepare a plant-based dish that serves at least 10 people. Don’t forget to include the recipe with ingredients listed so guests can remake your recipe at home. Plant-based only: No animal-based products (that includes meat, chicken, fish. Watch out for chicken broth, fish/bonita flakes and bacon bits) No dairy (butter, cheese, milk, etc.), egg, or honey 🥬 Plant-based curious or not a cook? No problem! Join in by bringing something simple like: (make sure you bring enough for 10 people) Fruit Veggies with hummus or baba ghanoush Pita chips and salsa A mix of nuts and olives 🗣️ Let’s Talk Food & Community: Throughout the evening, you’re invited to share the meal, engage in thoughtful conversation about your plant-based journey, food, sustainability, and the role plant-based choices can play in building a healthier future—for ourselves and our planet. Come hungry for more than just great food—come ready to connect, learn, and grow! 💚 Must register to hold your spot.

title: Cooking with Confidence: The Confident Cook
location: Center for Health and Wellbeing, 2005 Mizell Ave #800, Winter Park
description: Essential Skills for Everyday Cooking Presented by 4Root’s Culinary Health Institute at Center for Health & Wellbeing Build the skills that make cooking easier, more enjoyable, and more delicious. Join chef and food scientist , Erik Amnott , for an interactive culinary demonstration focused on the essential techniques every home cook can use to feel more confident in the kitchen. From mastering your knife skills to bringing out the best flavor in everyday ingredients, Erik will demonstrate practical techniques you can put to use right away, including: Essential knife skills and food preparation Blanching, grilling, roasting, and marinating vegetables Preparing starches on the stovetop Building and layering flavor Proper handling and measuring techniques Throughout the demonstration, you’ll have the opportunity to ask questions, learn practical nutrition insights, and discover how a few foundational skills can completely change the way you approach cooking. Guests will enjoy a sample of the finished dish and leave with a recipe to recreate at home. About Erik Erik Amnott combines food, health, and the environment to engage communities about the importance of urban agriculture and regenerative food systems. Using research and advocacy around non-ultra processed foods, Erik teaches the art of foraging, fermentation, and local food sourcing. Erik’s dedication to providing culinary education, alternative techniques for using locally sourced food, and building flavors have been the cornerstone of his classes. What You’ll Experience Hands-on culinary learning with Chef Erik Essential kitchen techniques you can use every day Practical ways to build and layer flavor Tips for proper preparation, handling, and measuring Conversation and Q&A with Chef Erik throughout the demonstration Event Details 📍 Location: Center for Health & Wellbeing – Nutrition Theatre: 2005 Mizell Ave, Winter Park, FL 32792 📅 Date: Tuesday, October 27 | 6:00PM – 7:00 PM 🎟️ Ticket Fee: $35

title: Make & Take: Strawberry Pot Painting Workshop
location: 4Roots Farm Campus, 1101 N. John Young Parkway, Parkway Orlando
description: Join us at the 4Roots Farm Campus for a hands-on Make & Take Workshop that brings the beauty of the farm straight to your home — perfect for anyone looking to add a splash of color and a taste of sweetness to the season! During this interactive class, you’ll learn how to paint and personalize your very own terracotta pot, then plant a fresh strawberry plant to make it truly yours. Our team will guide you step-by-step through decorating techniques, color combinations, and planting tips to help your strawberries thrive. We’ll kick things off with a short presentation showing how to paint the pots and how we care for our strawberry plants here on the farm, giving you a peek behind the scenes. Then it’s your turn to get creative: each participant will paint one pot, plant their own strawberry plant, and go home with everything they need to watch it grow — perfect for the Florida season! Event Details 🗓️ Thursday, October 29th | 6:00pm – 7:00pm 📍 4Roots Farm Campus – Education Building: 1101 N. John Young Pkwy, Orlando, FL 32804 🎟️ $30 Admission 🌿 All materials & supplies included! Please Note: Anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an adult. About the Make & Take Workshop Series Make & Take Workshops are monthly, beginner-friendly, hands-on experiences hosted by the 4Roots Farm team, designed to introduce our community to creative, sustainable DIY crafts inspired by nature. 🌿 Each workshop highlights an accessible, eco-friendly activity: from natural dyeing to botanical art and more, using materials sourced right here on the farm. Open to all ages, these sessions invite guests to learn new skills, explore the beauty of natural resources, and leave with a handmade creation to take home. Please Note: Anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an adult. 💚 Thank You for Supporting Our Mission 4Roots is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization dedicated to unearthing the power of food to build healthy communities. With your ticket purchase, you empower programs that connect people to fresh, nutritious food and education. Together, we can transform how communities think about, access, and interact with food. Each experience is designed to build practical skills while fostering a greater understanding of sustainability, engineering, and the natural world. 🌱 November’s Theme: Our Agrarian Roots Step back in time and explore the fields, forests and farms that helped shape the Sunshine State! title: Homeschool Day at 4Roots Farm (Ages 8-11)
location: 4Roots Farm Campus, 1101 N. John Young Parkway, Parkway Orlando
description: The 4Roots Homeschool Days program brings learning to life through hands-on experiences in the garden and beyond. Through seasonal, interactive activities, students explore agriculture and the environment in a way that encourages curiosity, creativity, and real-world connection. Designed for a range of ages, our program blends playful discovery with meaningful learning as students dive deeper into agriculture and related sciences. Each experience is designed to build practical skills while fostering a greater understanding of sustainability, engineering, and the natural world. December | Agriculture Around the World Learn about the Agricultural revolution and all the different ways agriculture came to be. Students will explore early crops, the first domesticated animals, and discover the techniques our ancestors used to plant, harvest, and thrive. Session activities: 🌿Simulate life as a hunter and gatherer 💧Learn about early irrigation methods in the Fertile Crescent 🐑 Explore early domestication of animals and the value they provided 🪷Experiment with alternative agricultural practices and create their own chinampa (floating garden) or hanging garden.

title: Origin | Splendor
location: 4Roots Farm Campus, 1101 N. John Young Parkway, Parkway Orlando
description: Origin invites guests to experience not simply what is on the plate, but everything that came before it. Nestled among the gardens and fields of the 4Roots Farm Campus, Origin is an intimate dining experience where the story of every remarkable meal begins. In partnership with a celebrated guest chef, a local farmer, and 4Roots’ Chef Hari Pulapaka, each dinner is a unique exploration of the season—never repeated, and rooted in what the land has to offer at that moment. Origin is more than fine dining. It is an invitation to experience food with a deeper sense of wonder. Not simply where food is served. But where its story begins.
